candidates.title: input fields inside ComboBoxOptions doesn't go into focus when clicked
candidates.origin: repo:tailwindlabs/headlessui is:issue is:closed upgrade keyboard in:title,body,comments
candidates.reason: Maintainer explicitly says additional input inside ComboboxOptions was inaccessible/unsupported even in v1; excluded P22 supported-baseline rule.
candidates.issueBody:
**What package within Headless UI are you using?**
@headlessui/react

**What version of that package are you using?**
v2.2.0

**What browser are you using?**
Brave, Chrome, Firefox

**Reproduction URL**
https://github.com/se-omar/combobox-bug

**Describe your issue**
I'm using the autocomplete combobox component, and I need to add an input field below all the options like the below snippet
```
<ComboboxOptions anchor="bottom" className="border empty:invisible">
    {filteredPeople.map((person) => (
	<ComboboxOption key={person.id} value={person} className="data-[focus]:bg-blue-100">
	    {person.name}
	</ComboboxOption>
    ))}
	    <input // <<<---- this input doesn't focus when clicked
		onClick={() => { console.log('clicked') }}
		onFocus={() => { console.log('focused') }}
		className='bg-white text-black rounded-md border border-gray-900' type="text"
	    />
</ComboboxOptions>
```
this functionality worked fine in v1.7, but since upgrading to v2, when clicking the input, it doesn't go into focus, the focus stays on the original `ComboBoxInput`, I found a hack to fix this by manually focusing the input on click
```
  <input // <<<---- now the input will focus
		onClick={(e) => { e.target.focus() }}
		onFocus={() => { console.log('focused') }}
		className='bg-white text-black rounded-md border border-gray-900' type="text"
	    />
```
I also recorded a video for reproduction: https://jam.dev/c/d9e24fe6-641a-478c-be6e-4a0d6b513405

comments.body:
Same issue after version updated. My template in ComboboxOption does not work for onClick evet. ```
{ addToFavorites(e, item, !isFavorite) }} > ...
```

Hey!

It looks like you are using the `Combobox` component not for its intended purposes. Adding another element like an `input` inside the `ComboboxOptions` won't make it accessible because you won't be able to reach it via the keyboard.

I totally get that it worked in v1, but even there it was not accessible and intended to be used like this.

What's the use case for adding an additional input _inside_ the Combobox? I would recommend to move it outside and render once an item is selected. If your use case is allowing to select *any* option instead of one from the list, then you can create a custom option based on the current input value.

More info about that use case can be found here: https://headlessui.com/react/combobox#allowing-custom-values

Going to close this as this is not something we support.

candidates.title: ComboBox single-select: after selection is done, input field gets focus
candidates.origin: repo:tailwindlabs/headlessui is:issue is:closed upgrade keyboard in:title,body,comments
candidates.reason: Maintainer explains intended input focus restoration and mobile improvement; no same-package stable regression/fix for reported behavior.
candidates.issueBody:
**What package within Headless UI are you using?**

@headlessui/vue

**What version of that package are you using?**

v1.7.19

**What browser are you using?**

Safari and Firefox

**Reproduction URL**

See #2795

**Describe your issue**

If you have a single-select ComboBox and select an option, the option list closes but the input element receives focus.

This has various implications:
* in terms of user experience, it looks like selection hasn't been finished (caret is blinking for non-obvious reasons)
* if mouse was used to open option list and select an option, it's unclear for user why input element gets focus out of a sudden
* with virtual keyboards, this behaviour is even more irritating, so #2272 tries to detect that, not setting focus in this case 
* detection of virtual keyboards is not safe, see remarks at #2272
* if ComboBox is the only input element on page, there is a blinking caret once user has finished selection, and there is no way to get rid of the caret; this is ugly
* for some applications, this behaviour even breaks application logic (see #2795)

Actually, I don't see any use case of this "set focus on input element" behaviour for single-select lists.

I suggest one of the following solutions:

* make this focus behaviour optional (actually, for mobiles it is already disabled)
* disable this behaviour completely for single-select lists

comments.body:
Hey!

We made some improvements to the Combobox component for Headless UI v2, this is currently not yet implemented in Vue yet, but you can play with the behavior in the React version. E.g.: open this on your phone: https://headlessui-react.vercel.app/combobox/combobox-countries

The main reason we re-focus the `ComboboxInput` is that you can continue from the current point, and go to the next field if there are any. If we don't re-focus the input then nothing would be focused (which typically means that the `body` is focused). If you use <kbd>tab</kbd> on desktop or use assistive technology on mobile then you would have to start from the top of the form again (because the `body` had focus).

Now, I do agree that it feels weird that the keyboard closes, it re-focuses the `combobox` and it opens your virtual keyboard again on mobile.

The improvements we made basically means that we never leave the focus of the `Combobox`. So there is no flash of your keyboard hiding and showing again. This behavior feels much better (similar to how you can type in a normal `input` and once you are done typing you are still focused in the `input` and you can continue to the next field if you want).

So to summarise, right now we never move focus away from the `ComboboxInput` which feels much better from a UX perspective _and_ solves a lot of issues that are no issues anymore.

Hope this helps!

Hey @RobinMalfait! We had the same issue after upgrading to headless ui v2 and I thought about a better pattern here would be to focus on the ComboboxButton after one option is selected for the single-select use case, that way the tab order is not lost and there is also opportunity to trigger the options list from keyboard. I made a hacky solution with setTimeout and references to button and input but would be great to have that behavior as an option in the Combobox component.

comments.body:
The problem lies in <CommandItem> from `shadcn`, as you said in `cmdk` version `1.0.0` they fixed some issues with data-value selector.

In the CommandItem that is created by default come with this classes:
`relative flex cursor-default select-none items-center rounded-sm px-2 py-1.5 text-sm outline-none aria-selected:bg-accent aria-selected:text-accent-foreground data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none data-[disabled]:opacity-50`

You need to remove the `data-disabled` related: 
`data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none`: this one disable all cursor events listening
`data-[disabled]:opacity-50`: this one put the text as disabled (only visual efect)
That fixed it, thanks @thelivingchaos

candidates.title: Let Escape close popups that mark each other when a dialog in another root has the same id
candidates.origin: repo:ariakit/ariakit is:issue is:closed regression keyboard in:title,body,comments
candidates.reason: Fix7732 identified, pre-existing root-collision case, no working stable baseline established; source preview packages are not a stable pair.
candidates.issueBody:
## Context

A review comment on #7719, which fixes #7647, found a case where the new rule for popups that mark each other reads a mark as the mark of the wrong dialog: https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/pull/7719#discussion_r4174143834.

## Problem

#7719 keeps the open dialogs in one order for the whole module, and it finds the owner of a mark through the dialog id:

```ts
for (const { current: openDialog } of openDialogs) {
  // ...
  if (!isElementMarked(dialog, openDialog.id)) continue;
  if (openedAfterDialog) return true;
  // ...
}
```

Ids are unique only in their root (a document or a shadow root). Suppose two popups in the document mark each other, and a dialog in another root has the same explicit id as the popup that opened first and opens after both. The lookup then reads the mark that the first popup set on the last popup as a mark from the dialog in the other root. That dialog opened later, so the last popup rejects <kbd>Escape</kbd>. The first popup rejects it too, and the pair stays stuck.

```tsx
<>
  <Ariakit.Dialog id="notice" open={open} modal={false} hideOnInteractOutside={false}>
    Notice
  </Ariakit.Dialog>
  <Ariakit.ComboboxProvider>
    <Ariakit.Combobox />
    <Ariakit.ComboboxPopover>{/* items */}</Ariakit.ComboboxPopover>
  </Ariakit.ComboboxProvider>
  {createPortal(
    // The same id in another root, open after the listbox.
    <Ariakit.Dialog id="notice" open={shadowOpen} modal={false} hideOnEscape={false}>
      Shadow notice
    </Ariakit.Dialog>,
    shadowRoot,
  )}
</>
```

With default props, the dialog in the other root is not marked by the document popups, so it accepts the first <kbd>Escape</kbd> and closes. The pair then closes in order with #7719. The pair stays stuck only while the dialog in the other root stays open, for example with `hideOnEscape={false}`.

A filter by root node is not a correct fix. A first attempt in #7719 skipped the open dialogs whose `getRootNode()` differs from the root of the given dialog, and its pre-commit review found a regression: a portaled popup in the document sets ancestor marks on a dialog in a shadow root that contains its disclosure, because the default portal is `document.body` and the walk also starts from the disclosure. With the filter, a dialog in a shadow-root app closed before its own open listbox. The fix must keep such marks and still not read a mark through an id that another root reuses.

## Pre-existing on main

The stuck state is pre-existing on `main`. A happy-dom probe on `main` at [`465d713`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/commit/465d713a1520eff26dce480acf5550ec221e0e6d) kept the Notice dialog and the listbox open after two <kbd>Escape</kbd> presses, both without and with the same-id dialog open in a shadow root, because that is #7647 itself. With `hideOnEscape={false}` on the dialog in the shadow root, all three stayed open. With the Notice dialog closed, one <kbd>Escape</kbd> closed the listbox.

The gap described here, the lookup of a mark owner through an id that another root reuses, exists only in the #7719 branch. This follow-up must wait for #7719 to merge.

## Why #7719 can finish without it

#7719 fixes the reported compositions. This case needs a duplicate explicit id across two roots, two popups that mark each other, and a dialog in the other root that opens last and stays open. It is not a regression: the same state is stuck on `main`.

## Expected outcome

A dialog in another root that reuses an id doesn't count as the owner of the marks of the dialog in this root, and a popup in another root that marks a dialog through its disclosure still counts. Tests cover both cases.

### Workaround

[Use distinct dialog IDs across roots (verified in Chrome)](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/7726#issuecomment-5978287510)

comments.body:
**Outcome: `ariakit-bug`.** Confirmed in Chrome on current `origin/main` at [`613dca2`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/commit/613dca23fcf488b2f78b381b27a5bde48a5e2306), after #7719 merged. `Dialog` and `ComboboxPopover` expose this behavior through `@ariakit/react`. Keep `bug`, `a11y`, and `p2`: the failure blocks keyboard dismissal, but needs a later-open dialog in another root that reuses an explicit ID and stays open. The fix has medium difficulty because it must preserve valid marks across roots.

I used a temporary `app/src/sandbox/dialog-7726/index.react.tsx` fixture, ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm dev-app`, and checked `/react/previews/dialog-7726/` on the worktree's Astro server with Playwright CLI and trusted keys. The shadow dialog's disclosure was in its own shadow root. The sequence opened Notice in the document, opened Drink with two ArrowDown presses, opened Shadow notice last, returned focus to Drink, and pressed Escape:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Both dialogs use `id="notice"`; shadow dialog has `hideOnEscape={false}` | All three popups remain open after three Escape presses. |
| Shadow dialog uses `id="shadow-notice"`; other props stay the same | First Escape closes Drink; second closes Notice; Shadow notice stays open. |
| Same ID, with Escape enabled on the shadow dialog | Three presses close Shadow notice, Drink, then Notice. |
| No open shadow dialog | Two presses close Drink, then Notice. |
| Same ID, with `unmountOnHide` on the listbox | Two presses close Drink, then Notice; Shadow notice stays open in this fixture. |

The root cause remains in [`hasDialogAbove`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/blob/613dca23fcf488b2f78b381b27a5bde48a5e2306/packages/ariakit-react-components/src/dialog/utils/__open-dialogs.ts#L31). The open order is shared across roots, but the mark lookup uses `openDialog.id`. The live DOM has the document Notice's mark on the listbox's ancestor. The later shadow dialog does not add that mark, yet its matching ID makes the lookup treat it as the owner. Because it opened later, the listbox rejects Escape. Notice also rejects Escape because the listbox marks it. `hideOnEscape={false}` keeps the shadow dialog in the open order, so the false match persists.

The [review reply](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/pull/7719#discussion_r4174380736) explains why a filter by `getRootNode()` would lose valid marks: a popup portaled to the document can mark a shadow-root dialog through its disclosure. The fix must identify the actual mark owner and preserve that case.

**Verified workaround:** Use distinct explicit IDs across roots for these dialogs. For example, change the shadow dialog's ID while leaving the document dialog as `id="notice"`:

```tsx
createPortal(
  <Ariakit.Dialog
    id="shadow-notice"
    open={shadowOpen}
    modal={false}
    hideOnEscape={false}
  >
    Shadow notice
  </Ariakit.Dialog>,
  shadowRoot,
);
```

`unmountOnHide` also worked in this fixture. Its mounting and open-order limits are documented in the [existing workaround](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/7647#issuecomment-5971691552).

With the same ID, all three popups stay open after two Escape presses:

![Notice, Drink, and Shadow notice remain open after two Escape presses](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e99c299-aca5-4f66-a86e-e8372dbfda2f)

With distinct IDs, the same two presses close Drink and Notice, while Shadow notice stays open:

![Only Shadow notice remains open after two Escape presses with distinct IDs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4770e265-0698-4cb4-af98-0f06bcfed88d)

The recording compares the same-ID failure with the distinct-ID workaround:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d84aed31-558d-495e-82ab-05ec505a8a5b

[Open the user-facing StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-99wcbut8?file=src%2FApp.tsx).

1. Select **Open Notice**.
2. Focus **Drink** and press **ArrowDown** twice.
3. Select **Open Shadow notice**, then return focus to **Drink**.
4. Press **Escape** twice. Notice, Drink, and Shadow notice all stay open.

Select **Use distinct IDs (workaround)** to reset the example, then repeat the steps. Escape closes Drink and Notice. Shadow notice stays open. The checkbox changes the shadow dialog from `id="notice"` to `id="shadow-notice"`. See the [triage comment](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/7726#issuecomment-5978287510) for the source diagnosis and workaround code.

I verified both cases in the in-app browser. The example uses public `@ariakit/react` components and pinned preview packages that include the merged changes from [#7719](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/pull/7719). The README lists the package versions. The **Let Escape close Shadow notice** option also lets users compare the default Escape behavior.

![Saved StackBlitz reproduction with all three popups open after two Escape presses](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae1f544e-db4d-48c7-8dc7-af153399b3e0)

<!-- issue-fixed-pr-7732 -->
This issue has been fixed and will be included in the next release.

If you'd like to try it now, you can install the canary version:

    npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@ariakit/react@7732

    npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@ariakit/react-components@7732

candidates.title: fireClickEvent's PointerEvent construction throws under vitest's jsdom environment: "Failed to construct 'PointerEvent': member view is not of type Window"
candidates.origin: repo:ariakit/ariakit is:issue is:closed upgrade keyboard in:title,body,comments
candidates.reason: JSDOM PointerEvent test environment, not frozen real browser user task.
candidates.issueBody:
### Current behavior

Since `@ariakit/utils` 0.2.0 (pulled in transitively by `@ariakit/react` 0.4.38+ via `@ariakit/react-components` 0.5.0+), every keyboard activation (<kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>) of a component built on `Command` — `Button`, `MenuButton`, `MenuItem`, `ToolbarItem`, etc. — silently fails inside a Vitest test that uses `environment: 'jsdom'`. The `onClick` handler never runs, `Menu`/`Combobox` popups never open, and Vitest reports an **unhandled exception** (it doesn't even surface as a normal assertion failure, since the throw happens inside a `queueMicrotask` callback):

```
TypeError: Failed to construct 'PointerEvent': member view is not of type Window.
 ❯ new UIEventImpl node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/events/UIEvent-impl.js:14:15
 ❯ new PointerEventImpl node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/events/PointerEvent-impl.js:5:1
 ❯ Object.exports.setup node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/generated/PointerEvent.js:58:12
 ❯ new PointerEvent node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/generated/PointerEvent.js:116:22
 ❯ fireClickEvent node_modules/@ariakit/utils/dist/index.js:822:16
 ❯ click node_modules/@ariakit/react-components/dist/command/command.js:73:26
```

A plain native `<button onClick>` activated the same way (Tab + Space/Enter through `@testing-library/user-event`) works fine, because the browser/jsdom dispatches the click itself rather than going through `fireClickEvent`.

### Steps to reproduce the bug

Minimal standalone repro (outside any existing project):

```sh
mkdir ariakit-repro && cd ariakit-repro
npm init -y
npm install --no-audit --no-fund \
  react@19 react-dom@19 \
  vitest@4.1.11 jsdom@27.4.0 \
  @testing-library/react @testing-library/user-event@14.6.6 \
  @vitejs/plugin-react @ariakit/react@0.4.38 \
  -D @testing-library/jest-dom
```

`vitest.config.mjs`:

```js
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import {defineConfig} from 'vitest/config'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts'],
  },
})
```

`vitest.setup.ts`:

```ts
import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'
```

`repro.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import * as A from '@ariakit/react'
import {render, screen} from '@testing-library/react'
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event'
import {expect, test, vi} from 'vitest'

test('ariakit Button: tab + Enter fires click', async () => {
  const fn = vi.fn()
  render(<A.Button onClick={fn}>ak</A.Button>)
  await userEvent.tab()
  await userEvent.keyboard('[Enter]')
  expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
})

test('ariakit Menu: tab + Space opens', async () => {
  render(
    <A.MenuProvider>
      <A.MenuButton>open</A.MenuButton>
      <A.Menu>
        <A.MenuItem>one</A.MenuItem>
      </A.Menu>
    </A.MenuProvider>,
  )
  await userEvent.tab()
  await userEvent.keyboard('[Space]')
  expect(screen.getByRole('menu')).toBeInTheDocument()
})

test('plain button: tab + Space fires click (control, not affected)', async () => {
  const fn = vi.fn()
  render(<button onClick={fn}>native</button>)
  await userEvent.tab()
  await userEvent.keyboard('[Space]')
  expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
})
```

Run:

```sh
npx vitest run
```

**Result on `@ariakit/react@0.4.38`** (`@ariakit/utils@0.2.0`, `@ariakit/react-components@0.5.0`) — 2 of 3 tests fail, plus 2 unhandled exceptions:

```
 ❯ repro.test.tsx (3 tests | 1 failed) 171ms
   × ariakit Menu: tab + Space opens 72ms

⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
 FAIL  repro.test.tsx > ariakit Menu: tab + Space opens
Error: [getByRole('menu')] Unable to find an accessible element ...

⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Errors ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
Vitest caught 2 unhandled errors during the test run.

TypeError: Failed to construct 'PointerEvent': member view is not of type Window.
 ❯ new UIEventImpl node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/events/UIEvent-impl.js:14:15
 ❯ new PointerEventImpl node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/events/PointerEvent-impl.js:5:1
 ❯ Object.exports.setup node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/generated/PointerEvent.js:58:12
 ❯ new PointerEvent node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/generated/PointerEvent.js:116:22
 ❯ fireClickEvent node_modules/@ariakit/utils/dist/index.js:822:16
 ❯ click node_modules/@ariakit/react-components/dist/command/command.js:73:26
[... second, identical error from the Space/keyup path at command.js:103:24 ...]

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
     Errors  2 errors
```

**Same test file re-run against `@ariakit/react@0.4.37`** (`npm install @ariakit/react@0.4.37`, resolving `@ariakit/utils@0.1.6` / `@ariakit/react-components@0.4.1`) — all 3 tests pass:

```
 RUN  v4.1.11 /private/tmp/ariakit-repro

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Expected behavior

Keyboard activation of `Command`-based components (`Button`, `MenuButton`, `MenuItem`, etc.) should fire the synthetic click and run `onClick` under Vitest + jsdom, the same way it does in a real browser and the same way it did on `@ariakit/react@0.4.37` / `@ariakit/utils@0.1.6`.

### Workaround

None found that doesn't require patching `@ariakit/utils` (e.g. via `pnpm.patchedDependencies` / `patch-package`) or pinning to `@ariakit/react@0.4.37`. Rendering the component on its default native `<button>` element and relying on the browser/jsdom's own click dispatch (rather than `Command`'s synthetic click path) avoids the crash, but that isn't viable for every use (e.g. `MenuButton`/`MenuItem` non-button renders, or components deliberately rendered as `<div>`/`<a>`).

https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/7395#issuecomment-5545176071

### Possible solutions

#### Root cause

`@ariakit/utils@0.2.0`'s `fireClickEvent` (`packages/ariakit-utils/src/events.ts`, compiled to `node_modules/@ariakit/utils/dist/index.js:797-823`) was changed to build a `PointerEvent` (falling back to `MouseEvent`) with a `view` member set to the element's owner window, via `getWindow(element)`:

```js
function getClickEventInit(view, eventInit) {
  const init = eventInit ?? {};
  return new Proxy({}, { get(_target, key) {
    if (key === "view") return view;
    if (key === "composed") return true;
    if (key === "pointerId") return init.pointerId ?? -1;
    if (key === "pointerType") return init.pointerType ?? "";
    if (hasOwnProperty(resetAttributes, key)) return void 0;
    return Reflect.get(init, key);
  } });
}

function fireClickEvent(element, eventInit) {
  const view = getWindow(element);
  const event = new (view.PointerEvent ?? view.MouseEvent)("click", getClickEventInit(view, eventInit));
  return element.dispatchEvent(event);
}
```

This is a deliberate fix for issue #7171 ("`fireClickEvent` dispatches synthetic clicks as `MouseEvent`, but browsers dispatch them as `PointerEvent`") and its follow-up #7192 ("The synthetic click behind keyboard activation reports `view: null` and `composed: false`"), verified against real browsers (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit via Playwright). In a real browser, `getWindow(element)` (`packages/ariakit-utils/src/dom.ts`) returns `element.ownerDocument.defaultView`, which is always a genuine `Window` instance, so constructing `new PointerEvent('click', {view, ...})` always succeeds there.

Under Vitest's `environment: 'jsdom'`, this assumption breaks. Vitest's jsdom environment setup copies the jsdom `window`'s properties onto Node's `globalThis` and then **rewrites `document.defaultView`** to return that same `globalThis` object instead of the original jsdom `Window` instance. From `vitest/dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js` (Vitest 4.1.11), inside the `populateGlobal` helper:

```js
global.window = global;
global.self = global;
global.top = global;
global.parent = global;
if (global.global) global.global = global;
// rewrite defaultView to reference the same global context
if (global.document && global.document.defaultView) Object.defineProperty(global.document, "defaultView", {
  get: () => global,
  enumerable: true,
  configurable: true
});
```

As a result, in every Vitest test running under `environment: 'jsdom'`:

```js
document.defaultView === window   // true
window === globalThis             // true
document.defaultView instanceof Window   // false — globalThis is not a jsdom Window instance
```

confirmed with a diagnostic test against this exact setup:

```
stdout | diagnostic.test.ts > ...
document.defaultView === window: true
window === globalThis: true
document.defaultView instanceof Window: false
```

`getWindow(element)` therefore returns `globalThis` rather than a true jsdom `Window`. jsdom's own WebIDL conversion for `UIEventInit.view` (used by both `PointerEvent` and `MouseEvent`, since `PointerEvent` extends `MouseEvent` extends `UIEvent`) requires that value to satisfy `instanceof Window` in jsdom's realm, and `globalThis` does not, so the constructor throws:

```js
new PointerEvent('click', {view: window})                         // throws "member view is not of type Window"
new MouseEvent('click', {view: document.defaultView})              // throws, same reason
new PointerEvent('click', {view: null})                            // OK
```

**This is jsdom correctly rejecting a value that fails its WebIDL check, not an Ariakit bug in the WebIDL sense** — the underlying issue is that Vitest's `populateGlobal` rewrite makes `document.defaultView` (and therefore whatever `getWindow()` returns) something jsdom's own event constructors don't recognize as their own `Window`. `@ariakit/utils` has no visibility into that rewrite; it is just the first code path that happens to pass `getWindow(element)` into a jsdom event constructor as `view`.

#### Suggested fix

Three options were considered:

1. **Try/catch fallback**: in `fireClickEvent`, attempt to construct the event with `view` set, and on failure, construct again without `view` (or with `view: null`).
2. **Guard with `instanceof Window`**: only pass `view` when `view instanceof view.Window` (i.e., confirm the resolved window is actually an instance of its own `Window` constructor before using it as `view`), falling back to omitting `view` otherwise.
3. **Drop `view` from `getClickEventInit` entirely**, keeping `getWindow(element)` only to pick the constructor (`view.PointerEvent ?? view.MouseEvent`), and let the browser/jsdom default `view` to `null`/`undefined` for the synthetic click, matching the pre-0.2.0 behavior for this member.

**Recommendation: option 2, with option 1 as a safety net.** Option 3 undoes the part of the #7192 fix that made the synthetic click report the element's own window as `view` (matching real-browser behavior), which is presumably wanted for consumers who read `event.view`. Option 2 keeps that behavior everywhere it already works (real browsers, and any DOM implementation where the resolved window passes its own `instanceof Window` check) and only degrades gracefully in the one situation where `getWindow()`'s result isn't recognized as a `Window` by the environment's own constructors — which is exactly the situation Vitest's jsdom environment creates. A bare try/catch (option 1) is simpler but silently swallows any other WebIDL rejection reason too, so pairing an explicit `instanceof` guard with a narrow try/catch fallback (for engines where `instanceof Window` isn't a reliable enough check) seems like the most robust combination. Either way, the fix belongs in `fireClickEvent`/`getClickEventInit` in `@ariakit/utils`, since that's the shared helper other `fire*Event` functions (`fireEvent`, `fireBlurEvent`, `fireFocusEvent`, `fireKeyboardEvent`) also rely on `getWindow()` for — worth checking whether any of those construct events with a `view`-like member too.

We are not asking Ariakit to work around Vitest's specific `populateGlobal` rewrite by name — just to not throw when the window `getWindow()` resolves isn't recognized as a `Window` instance by the very constructors it's about to be passed into.

---

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| `@ariakit/react` | 0.4.38 (bug present); 0.4.37 (last good) |
| `@ariakit/utils` (transitive) | 0.2.0 (bug present, released 2026-08-24); 0.1.6 (last good) |
| `@ariakit/react-components` (transitive) | 0.5.0 (bug present); 0.4.1 (last good) |
| React | 19.2.8 |
| Vitest | 4.1.11 |
| jsdom | 27.4.0 |
| `@testing-library/react` | 16.3.3 |
| `@testing-library/user-event` | 14.6.6 |
| `@vitejs/plugin-react` | 6.1.1 |
| Node.js | 24.18.0 |
| OS | macOS (Darwin) |

`@ariakit/react@0.4.39` (released 2026-09-02) still depends on `@ariakit/react-components@0.6.0` → `@ariakit/utils@0.2.0`, so it is still affected as of this writing.

---

## Prior-art check (done before filing)

Searched `gh search issues --repo ariakit/ariakit` and `gh search prs --repo ariakit/ariakit` for: `PointerEvent`, `member view is not of type Window`, `jsdom`, `fireClickEvent`, `vitest`, `Failed to construct`, `PointerEvent view Window`, `0.2.0 regression`, `keyboard activation vitest`, `defaultView`, `@ariakit/utils 0.2.0`, plus a listing of all issues opened since 2026-08-24 (the `@ariakit/utils@0.2.0` release date).

Found and read the issues that produced the `fireClickEvent` change (all closed, all fixed and released in 0.2.0):

- **#7171** — "`fireClickEvent` dispatches synthetic clicks as `MouseEvent`, but browsers dispatch them as `PointerEvent`" (fixed by PR #7189).
- **#7192** — "The synthetic click behind keyboard activation reports `view: null` and `composed: false`" (fixed by PR #7216) — this is the one that added `view` to `getClickEventInit`.
- **#7193** — "Event helpers in `@ariakit/utils` build events from the ambient global instead of the element's own window" (fixed by PR #7213) — same `getWindow()`-based approach applied to the other `fire*Event` helpers.
- **#7162**, **#7199**, **#7204**, **#7201**, **#7202**, **#7206**, **#7215**, **#7218**, **#7225**, **#7228** and others from the same late-August batch — all about realm/window resolution and browser-parity fixes (verified via Playwright against Chromium/Firefox/WebKit), none about a Vitest+jsdom `PointerEvent` construction failure.

None of these — nor any other issue or PR found — describes the specific regression reported here: `PointerEvent`/`MouseEvent` construction throwing under Vitest's jsdom environment because `document.defaultView`/`getWindow()` resolves to something that fails jsdom's own `instanceof Window` check. **This does not appear to be a known/reported issue as of 2026-09-02.**

---

*Reported from an isolated standalone reproduction; not derived from or affecting any private codebase.*

comments.body:
TLDR: Triage outcome: `third-party`.

I reproduced the report through the public `@ariakit/react` `Button` path and directly through `@ariakit/utils/fireClickEvent` on current [`6cb59755f`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/commit/6cb59755fcecf62f4a0dd0a6e92662a2bc774ac9), using Node 24.18.0, Vitest 4.1.11, jsdom 27.4.0, React 19.2.8, and `@testing-library/user-event` 14.6.6. With Vitest's default `forks` pool, `onClick` received zero calls and Vitest reported the same unhandled exception from `fireClickEvent`:

```text
TypeError: Failed to construct 'PointerEvent': member view is not of type Window.
```

The direct helper check failed at the same constructor. Upgrading the isolated check to jsdom 30.0.1 did not change the result.

The failure comes from Vitest's non-VM jsdom environment. In the default pool, the diagnostic values were:

```text
document.defaultView === window: true
window === globalThis: true
window instanceof Window: false
```

Constructing the same event with a standalone jsdom window succeeds, including `view === jsdom.window`. Vitest rewrites `document.defaultView` to its Node global context, but jsdom's Web IDL conversion does not recognize that context as a jsdom `Window`. This is the same upstream behavior reported in [vitest-dev/vitest#4685](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/4685). A Vitest maintainer [describes it as expected for the non-VM pools](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/4685#issuecomment-1843178287) and [recommends `vmThreads`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/4685#issuecomment-1843383238).

I reran the current-main `Button` check with both `vmThreads` and `vmForks`. Both passed, and the VM diagnostic reported `window instanceof Window: true`. The direct workaround is:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: "jsdom",
    pool: "vmThreads",
  },
});
```

Vitest documents the [VM pool tradeoffs](https://vitest.dev/config/pool.html#vmthreads), so suites should account for its VM-realm and module-cache limitations. The pinning and native-host alternatives already documented in the [issue's Workaround section](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/7395#workaround) also remain valid.

The current Ariakit code supplies the owning window for `UIEventInit.view`, matching the real-browser behavior verified for #7192. The value becomes invalid only after Vitest substitutes a non-`Window` global context. I am therefore closing this as an upstream test-environment limitation rather than changing Ariakit's browser-parity behavior.
so, the workaround is to force every dev test environment to use `pool: 'vmThreads'` I'm not sure that this may be considered a viable workaround

candidates.origin: repo:ariakit/ariakit is:issue is:closed upgrade keyboard in:title,body,comments
candidates.reason: Fix7376 identified, pre-existing main finding, no working stable baseline established.
candidates.issueBody:
## Context

Found while reviewing [#7376](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/pull/7376), which originally fixed the opposite composition order tracked in #7364. This issue is the mirror case: the final `accessibleWhenDisabled` value comes from a `Focusable` below `CompositeItem`. Because both cases cross the same static collection-registration boundary, #7376 now fixes them together.

## Problem

[`CompositeItem`](https://ariakit.com/reference/composite-item) derives the disabled state it registers in the composite store from its own props and from the [`accessibleWhenDisabled`](https://ariakit.com/reference/focusable#accessiblewhendisabled) value it inherits from a composing layer above it. It does not see a value that a [`Focusable`](https://ariakit.com/reference/focusable) it renders below itself resolves.

When the inner `Focusable` keeps the element keyboard accessible, the rendered element is reachable but the store still registers the item as disabled. Arrow navigation therefore skips it.

```tsx
<Ariakit.CompositeProvider>
  <Ariakit.Composite role="listbox" aria-label="Inner override">
    <Ariakit.CompositeItem role="option">Inner one</Ariakit.CompositeItem>
    <Ariakit.CompositeItem
      disabled
      role="option"
      render={<Ariakit.Focusable accessibleWhenDisabled />}
    >
      Inner two
    </Ariakit.CompositeItem>
    <Ariakit.CompositeItem role="option">Inner three</Ariakit.CompositeItem>
  </Ariakit.Composite>
</Ariakit.CompositeProvider>
```

Clicking `Inner one` and pressing ArrowRight moves focus to `Inner three`. The item that the inner `Focusable` deliberately kept reachable is unavailable through arrow navigation.

## Verification

The finding is pre-existing on `main`. The same fixture failed against [`3d0e69ab2`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/commit/3d0e69ab2f2ca491472aedf54462191bf7a37ab0), which is an ancestor of `main` and the merge base of #7376, and against the earlier pull request head [`7c082a231`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/commit/7c082a2314a2237f59a057425cd843968b3aecee).

The final fix passes focused React 19, React 18, and Chromium tests. ArrowRight now reaches the accessible disabled item:

[Screen recording: ArrowRight reaches an accessible disabled item resolved below CompositeItem](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e2fbe60-9a42-4940-b266-4652f9045119)

![Focus is on Rendered two after ArrowRight reaches the accessible disabled item](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6ab4942-09cc-4e25-ac54-16089fa466cc)

## Pull request

[#7376](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/pull/7376) fixes both static composition orders. It uses the existing internal `data-truly-disabled` marker as a tri-state handoff. An active disabled `Focusable` stamps `"true"` when the element is truly disabled and `"false"` when it remains keyboard accessible. An inactive `Focusable` removes the marker. `CompositeItem` reads the exact value once during its existing collection registration effect and falls back to its own resolved state when the marker is absent.

`data-truly-disabled` is an internal implementation detail; consumer-authored values do not define supported behavior. The inactive `Focusable` guard keeps `disabled` with `focusable={false}` registered as disabled, with direct and inherited regression coverage. The implementation does not use a `MutationObserver`, rendered-node state, or a render-prop dependency. A value that changes only inside a nested `Focusable` after the item registered remains outside this fix.

## Expected outcome

`CompositeItem` registers the disabled state that the innermost active `Focusable` resolved, so the composite store and rendered element agree in both static composition orders.

## Workaround

For released versions that do not contain the fix, pass `accessibleWhenDisabled` on the `CompositeItem` itself, in addition to the inner `Focusable`:

```tsx
<Ariakit.CompositeItem
  disabled
  accessibleWhenDisabled
  role="option"
  render={<Ariakit.Focusable accessibleWhenDisabled />}
>
  Inner two
</Ariakit.CompositeItem>
```

You can remove the duplicate prop after upgrading to a release that contains the fix.
